### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **78** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-comment.object.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**50** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-comment.object.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 35 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 41 pages)`
- **15** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **150** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2696303da89b4821780b7fbc6eca9491d01aa196` — the merge of head `42b3638b946bdbbf42e5d5d9b1b87c7c7fc99f3e` into base `404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2696303da89b4821780b7fbc6eca9491d01aa196 && git checkout 2696303da89b4821780b7fbc6eca9491d01aa196
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc 42b3638b946bdbbf42e5d5d9b1b87c7c7fc99f3e && git checkout -B drift-repro 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc && git merge --no-ff 42b3638b946bdbbf42e5d5d9b1b87c7c7fc99f3e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `42b3638b946bdbbf42e5d5d9b1b87c7c7fc99f3e`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #23281 (body and all five comments: triage 6147772435, claim 6150488591, report 6152601447, amendment 6152677078, round-1 report 6153407686); PR #23318 body and its 12-file list; the net diff against `main` from merge base `5c9bfb0d3f` (12 files, +1521/−21, identical to the file list); and the 48 check-runs on the head — all completed, 41 success, 7 skipped, 0 failure, with `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` each `success`. No governed path; head repo is the base repo; 1,542 changed lines; draft, no auto-merge.

1. **New public CLI surface `os migrate comment-reactions`** (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/comment-reactions.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/comment-reactions-conversion.ts`) — additive. Flags `--database-url`, `--apply`, `--yes`, `--force`, `--json`; dry run by default; the `--json` document is `{ database, apply, report, check, verified, flag, duration }`; exit 1 while a value is unreadable, a write failed, or an `--apply` read-back is not clean. The shape is `audit-metadata-bodies`' (occupancy gate, confirmation, read-only boot with `deferSchemaDdl` and `readOnlyProbe`, `absentTableReads`) plus `value-shapes`' ledger row. Registered in both derived-population tables (`schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts`, `json-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts`), documented in `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` (table row and a subsection) and listed as a checklist variant. **Right.**

2. **Reads below the data door** through `engine.getDriverForObject(...).find` for `sys_comment` (`id`, `organization_id`, `reactions`) and for `sys_user` — the `account-issuer` precedent; keyset paging on `id`; no WHERE on the retired column, so a v18-created database that never had it reads clean (the one-shot family table drives both modes against such a database under `Test Core`). `sys_comment_reaction` is read through the engine with `context: { isSystem: true }`, and `context` is a declared query slot of `engine.find`. Neither the engine nor `SqlDriver.find` applies an implicit LIMIT, so the per-page `held` set is complete. **Right.**

3. **What is written:** one `sys_comment_reaction` row per distinct (comment, emoji, user), `created_by` = the reactor, `organization_id` = the comment's, under `{ isSystem: true, skipAutomations: true }`. In `comment-access-hooks.ts`, `onInsert` returns on `session.isSystem` before `authorizeReactionInsert` would stamp `user_id` from the session, so the stored reactor is kept; the own-record delete floor reads `created_by`, so a converted reaction is removable by its reactor. The declared `(comment_id, emoji, user_id)` index, `unique: 'organization'`, refuses duplicates, and the natural-key skip makes a re-run the resume (ablation 1 shows the index catching every duplicate once the guard is off). Unreadable values — `not_json`, `not_a_map`, `not_a_user_list`, `not_a_user_id`, `emoji_not_storable` (bound read from the registered `maxLength`), `unknown_user` — are listed with their comment id and converted into nothing, while the readable entries of the same map still convert. **Right.**

4. **New `sys_migration` ledger id `sys-comment-reactions-to-records`,** written through `recordDataMigrationRun` (`applied: true`; `passed` only when the writing run failed nothing and a read-only re-walk finds nothing left to convert and nothing unreadable; `blocking` = failures + unconverted + unreadable) and read through `readDataMigrationFlag` + `isDataMigrationFlagVerified`, the one arbiter. It fails toward retention: no `sys_migration` object, no row, an unreadable row and an unverified row all read `verified: false`. **Right.** Advisory, not blocking: a failed write is counted in `blocking` once as a failure and once as still-unconverted by the read-back; the gate compares `blocking` to zero only, so the over-count cannot flip it.

5. **Accept-set narrowing on `os migrate apply --allow-destructive`** (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts`): when `intended` holds exactly `drop_column` of `sys_comment.reactions`, the command refuses — human face exit 1; `--json` exit 1 with `message: "refused_comment_reactions_unconverted"`, `detail`, `conversion` (the ledger row or `null`), `applied: []`, `created: []` — until the verified row exists, and otherwise prints the verification date and proceeds. Placement: after the `sys_account.issuer` pre-flight, above `totalIntended`, the confirmation prompt, `flushSchemaDdl()` and `applyMigrationEntries()`; the outer `catch` re-throws the exit signal. Without `--allow-destructive` the drop is deferred and the gate is never reached, so no other drift entry, flag or exit path moves. Reading the ledger rather than re-probing live is correct: a member may un-react after conversion, and a live probe would read that deleted row as unconverted. The seven-case integration pin (`comment-reactions.integration.test.ts`) walks refuse, dry run, apply, re-run, still refused, verified, drop, on one real SQLite file with the composition the served boot mounts. **Right.**

6. **Second narrowing in the same file:** the two `sys_account.issuer` pre-flight refusals under `--json` (`refused_account_issuer_collisions`, `refused_account_issuer_preflight_unreadable`) now hand `1` to `emitJson` instead of `0`; the document is unchanged and the human face already exited 1. A declared-but-unenforced refusal status fixed where it lives; `apply.account-issuer-json-refusal.test.ts` pins both with a human-face control and a clean-pre-flight control, and the recorded ablation reds both pins. **Right.**

7. **`packages/spec`:** the protocol-18 semantic entry `sys-comment-reactions-column-retired` changes in three prose fields (`replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`); `id` and `surface` unchanged; no `*.zod.ts`, authorable key, export or stored shape moves, so no committed generated artifact moves (the upgrade guide is generated into the gitignored `content/docs/protocol-upgrade/`, and `check:upgrade-guide` and `check:spec-changes` ran inside the green `TypeScript Type Check`). The `reason` text now records the 2026-10-10 ruling as permitting an unmigrated column and the 2026-10-13 rule as taking it up — the supersession the triage comment states; no Chinese ruling is quoted, so the verbatim-quote rule is not engaged. **Right.**

8. **`plugin-audit` `sys-comment.object.ts`:** docblock only, no runtime change. **Right.** **`cli.mdx`:** hand-written tree, existing page, no `meta.json` entry needed. **Right.** **`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json`:** revision 4 with 16 variants — the head's `commands/migrate/` holds exactly 16 non-test command modules besides `index.ts`, and the JSON parses. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23281-comment-reactions-upgrade-conversion.md`: `@objectstack/cli: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: patch`; summary `feat(cli)!:`; a **BREAKING** (accept-set narrowing) banner; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with its reason; the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (already-registered sys-comment-reactions-column-retired)` in the HTML-comment marker the registration gate reads; and the migration text a breaking changeset owes (convert, verify, then drop; what to do when the apply refuses). `Check Changeset` is green on the head (no `major` under the launch-window guard; the level axis satisfied), and the dev's `check:adr-0087-registration` reading is `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (already-registered)`.
- The spelling matches the lane's narrowing precedent exactly (`.changeset/23178-auth-gate-raw-host-families.md`, landed as `08b38cb9d8`): `minor` + bang + banner + `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` + a `not-required` disposition. The tree is in changeset pre mode (`.changeset/pre.json`, tag `next`; both packages at `18.0.0-next.0`), where `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` forbids a `major`, so `minor` carrying the breaking markers is the correct level for the CLI narrowing. **Right.**
- `@objectstack/spec` `patch` for prose-only fields of a semantic entry — nothing an author writes moves. **Right.** `plugin-audit` carries no changeset: a comment-only edit publishes nothing. **Right.** `skip-changeset` is correctly absent: cli and spec publish.
- **Clause-②:** `no (narrowing)` — in the changeset, in the PR body's opening lines, and in the claim as amended in place (6152677078). It matches the diff: the additions (a new subcommand, a new `sys_migration` row id) put no new key on a published payload, and the two narrowings are the apply refusal and the issuer exit status. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` is empty in both reports (6152601447, 6153407686). Every declared deviation, answered:

- R1-1 `apply.ts` outside the claim's file surface — **accepted** (adopted by the amendment); verified that the hunk fires only on the exact `sys_comment.reactions` drop inside `intended`, so apply's general behaviour is unchanged.
- R1-2 `utils/comment-reactions-conversion.ts`, both family tables, `cli.mdx` — **accepted**; each file is read above; the util sits outside `commands/` because oclif loads every module there.
- R1-3 no migration journal — **accepted**: each insert is atomic, the unique index and the natural-key skip make a re-run the resume, and the ledger row is the evidence the drop gate reads.
- R1-4 the measured database was main-created with the column and values planted by hand, not written by a 17.x release — **accepted with a residual**: the stored shape is confirmed against objectui's `storedReactions()` reader (`JSON.stringify` of an emoji-to-user-id map) and the parser also takes a driver-decoded object, but a database a 17.x release itself wrote has not been read through this command. That reading belongs to the cloud rehearsal that filed the card (objectstack-ai/cloud#2867, item I9) — flagged to the seat, not blocking here.
- R1-5 zero label writes — **fine**. R1-6 the model-free commit trailer pair — **fine**, AGENTS.md's form.
- R1-7 `json-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts` (nightly) gained the member and was not run locally — **accepted**: the per-PR one-shot family table drove the same command through `run()` under the green `Test Core`; the nightly's first run on `main` is the carrier.
- R2-1 the issuer pins are unit-tier with the boot, occupancy probe, process exit and pre-flight probe replaced — **accepted**: the real-door measurement (the collision case and the 200,001-row unreadable case) was taken and recorded before the change, the two controls tell a refusal from a run, and a 200,001-row fixture is not a per-PR pin.
- R2-2 the ADR-0087 disposition is an HTML comment — **right**: it is the one spelling the registration gate reads, and the precedent is spelled the same way.
- R2-3 `origin/main` not merged this round — **accepted**: `main` has since moved to `87e902dcbb` (15 files), none of them this PR's and none under `packages/cli/`; the PR reads `mergeable: true`, and the queue rebuilds on current `main` (§7).
- R2-4 `check:platform-checklist` exits 1 on 8 ABSENT SYMBOL anchors in `access-security.json`, `search.json` and `attachments-storage.json`, identical without this PR's edit and at `origin/main` — **outside this diff** (the decision recorded in `lint.yml` keeps that gate out of per-PR CI; its daily watchdog owns it) and **escalated**: the dev names no carrier beyond the watchdog, so the owning seat should confirm a main-red card exists for those 8 anchors or file one; this record files nothing (one write only).
- The two round-1 out-of-scope findings (the issuer `--json` exit codes; the stale 13-subcommand list) were pulled into round 1 by the amendment and are closed on this head.
- The advisory in ① item 4 (the `blocking` over-count on a failed write) is for the dev's next touch of the module; it does not move the verdict.

**VERDICT: PASS**
